Definition: from G3844 and G2064; to come near or aside, i.e. to approach (arrive), go by (or away), (figuratively) perish or neglect, (causative) avert:--come (forth), go, pass (away, by, over), past, transgress.
BiblicalUsage: Parerchomai means to pass by, to pass away, to go by. Jesus says in Matthew 24:35 that heaven and earth shall pass away, but His words shall not pass away. Paul says in 2 Corinthians 5:17 that if any man be in Christ, old things are passed away and all things are become new. Peter warns in 2 Peter 3:10 that the heavens shall pass away with a great noise, and the same word turns to service in Luke 12:37, where the master who finds his servants watching will come forth and serve them.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe everything passes except His word, and the passing is not an ending but a clearing: old things pass so new things can come. That is why I hold that the master who serves His watching servants is the hope that makes the waiting worth it.
RelatedTopics: End Times; New Creation; Second Coming
